definitions.explanation: Sake specifically intended for cooking rather than drinking. Used to remove odors from meat and fish, add flavor, and tenderize ingredients.

examples.japanese: {料理酒|りょうりしゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{大|おお}さじ→大さじ：22527_oosaji⟧⟦{一杯|いっぱい}→一杯：01793_ippai⟧⟦{加|くわ}える→加える：01941_kuwaeru⟧。
examples.english: Add one tablespoon of cooking sake.

examples.japanese: {料理酒|りょうりしゅ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{肉|にく}→肉：02240_niku⟧や⟦{魚|さかな}→魚：00499_sakana⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{臭|くさ}み⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: Cooking sake is used to remove the odor from meat and fish.

examples.japanese: {料理酒|りょうりしゅ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧とき⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{普通|ふつう}→普通：01502_futsuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日本酒|にほんしゅ}→日本酒：12954_nihonshu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{代用|だいよう}→代用：16439_daiyou⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: When you don't have cooking sake, you can substitute regular sake.

notes:
USAGE:
A staple seasoning in Japanese cooking alongside ⟦{醤油|しょうゆ}→醤油：01056_shouyu⟧ (soy sauce) and ⟦{味醂|みりん}→味醂：04918_mirin⟧ (sweet rice wine). {料理酒|りょうりしゅ} typically has salt added to make it undrinkable, which classifies it as a seasoning rather than an alcoholic beverage in Japan. This allows it to be sold without a liquor license.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {料理酒|りょうりしゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{加|くわ}える→加える：01941_kuwaeru⟧ (to add cooking sake)
- {料理酒|りょうりしゅ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{下味|したあじ}→下味：06809_shitaaji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つける→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧ (to season with cooking sake)
- {料理酒|りょうりしゅ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{醤油|しょうゆ}→醤油：01056_shouyu⟧ (cooking sake and soy sauce)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{味醂|みりん}→味醂：04918_mirin⟧: mirin, sweet rice wine — sweeter, used for glazing and sweetening
- ⟦{日本酒|にほんしゅ}→日本酒：12954_nihonshu⟧: sake — drinking sake, can also be used for cooking
